newsitem.title: CYPRUS: EU envoy sees progress on Cyprus dispute in 1997.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy sees progress on Cyprus dispute in 1997.

text.p: Greek and Turkish Cypriots in divided Cyprus are keen to start direct negotiations to broker a settlement on the divided island, an envoy from the trade bloc said on Tuesday.
"I was given categorical assurances both leaders are preparing for direct negotiations," said Kester Heaslip, the representative on Cyprus of Ireland's EU presidency's.

"They are anxious to engage in them," Heaslip told a news conference of Greek and Turkish Cypriot journalists in the divided capital of Nicosia. "They are prepared to enter these talks in good faith hoping to achieve a successful outcome."
Heaslip said he was optimistic direct talks, which have been rarely held, could start as early as March.

The Irish diplomat spent a week on the island meeting members of both communities to discuss the benefits of EU membership, and to explore the possibility of a settlement to the decades-old dispute in the coming months.
Cyprus, which applied for EU membership in 1990, is due to start accession negotiations with the bloc in early to mid 1998.
Its northern third has been occupied by Turkey since 1974 in an invasion sparked by a short-lived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.
International efforts to resolve the dispute and reunite Cyprus under a federal umbrella have gathered pace recently in view of the upcoming accession negotiations.
The Turkish Cypriot leadership, which declared a breakaway state in the north recognised only by Ankara in 1983, opposes Cypriot membership in the union.

It cites treaties stating that the island cannot become a member of a body Turkey or Greece -- both guarantor powers -- are not members of and says Cyprus's application was legally invalid because the views of Turkish Cypriots were not taken into account.
"Yes, that is his view," said Heaslip, referring to Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash. "But our position is that this need not be raised as an obstacle just now."
Cyprus's course to membership without achieving a solution will be "difficult", Heaslip said, though not impossible.
"We have to make the best of the situation....the EU will fulfill its engagement."
